svg.aria-label: Flowchart: a candidate execution E interleaving a PaymentRun worker and a settlement-ingest thread over CLIENT_BONUS_AVAILABLE and CLIENT_CASH_AVAILABLE must pass gate 1, happens-before consistency clause 1, and gate 2, happens-before consistency clause 2, failing either sends it to a rejected branch. Executions that pass both proceed to gate 3, the committed-action construction of JLS 17.4.8, which rejects an out-of-thin-air execution that satisfied both earlier clauses but has no causal justification. Executions surviving all three gates reach the DRF-SC exit: if every conflicting access is ordered by happens-before, every happens-before-consistent execution is sequentially consistent. A caveat attached to the exit states that one racy field anywhere in the program loses sequential-consistency reasoning in principle, because the guarantee is whole-program, not per-field.
svg.text: HAPPENS-BEFORE CONSISTENCY IS NOT ENOUGH — GATES A CANDIDATE EXECUTION MUST PASS
Candidate execution E
PaymentRun worker + settlement-ingest thread interleave reads/writes
over CLIENT_BONUS_AVAILABLE and CLIENT_CASH_AVAILABLE
GATE 1 — happens-before consistency, clause (1)
every action is consistent with the sequential program-order
semantics of its own thread — each read sees its thread's own
most recent prior write
REJECTED — clause (1) fails
settlement-ingest-2 reads a value its own
thread never wrote or observed via hb
GATE 2 — happens-before consistency, clause (2)
for every read r of a shared write w, no write w' exists with
w hb w' hb r on the same field — no read is skipped over by
an intervening happens-before write
REJECTED — clause (2) fails
operator-review reads a stale 180 though a
hb-ordered write already stored 260
GATE 3 — committed-action construction (JLS 17.4.8)
actions are added incrementally from a well-formed prefix;
each newly committed read must be justified by a write already
committed, or by a legal race — hb-consistency alone is not a
causal justification
REJECTED — out-of-thin-air
passed both hb-consistency clauses, yet a
PaymentRun worker reads CLIENT_BONUS_AVAILABLE
= 42 with no write order ever producing 42
— no causal justification exists
EXIT — DRF-SC
data-race-free implies sequential consistency
if every conflicting access in E is ordered by happens-before
(E is properly synchronized), then every happens-before-consistent
execution of E is sequentially consistent
caveat — the guarantee is all-or-nothing
One racy field anywhere in the program loses SC reasoning
in principle — DRF-SC is a whole-program property, not a
per-field one. One unsynchronized access to, say,
CLIENT_BONUS_AVAILABLE forfeits it for the whole execution.
candidate execution / gate
rejected branch
DRF-SC exit theorem
annotation / caveat panel
A → B : E passes gate A into gate B
A → B : E fails gate A, rejected as B
A → B : caveat attached to A
